items.name: Author's Purpose
items.copy:
Title: AUTHOR'S PURPOSE
Subtitle: Why did the author write this?
Five illustrated sections, each with its own clear heading, short explanation and example:
PERSUADE — Convince the reader. "Our school should plant a garden."
INFORM — Teach facts. "Seeds need water, air, and warmth."
ENTERTAIN — Tell an enjoyable story. "The airship raced into the storm!"
EXPLAIN — Show how or why. "First, soak the seeds. Next, plant them."
DESCRIBE — Help us picture it. "Pink roses covered the cool stone wall."
Bottom strip: LOOK AT THE WHOLE TEXT
Ask: What should I think, know, or feel?
Watch out: A text can have several purposes. Choose the MAIN one.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Text Structure
items.copy:
Title: TEXT STRUCTURE
Subtitle: How are the ideas organized?
DESCRIPTION — A topic with details. Clues: such as, including.
SEQUENCE — Steps or events in order. Clues: first, next, finally.
COMPARE & CONTRAST — Alike and different. Clues: both, unlike, however.
CAUSE & EFFECT — Why it happened and the result. Clues: because, so, as a result.
PROBLEM & SOLUTION — A difficulty and how it is fixed. Clues: problem, solve.
LITERARY STRUCTURE
Chapters build a novel. Scenes build a play. Stanzas build a poem.
Watch out: One signal word is only a clue. Check how MOST ideas connect.

items.name: Theme
items.copy:
Title: THEME
Subtitle: What life lesson does the story teach?
TOPIC: friendship
THEME: Friends help each other through difficult times.
Follow the clues:
CHALLENGE → RESPONSE → OUTCOME → LESSON
CHALLENGE: A heavy garden gate will not open.
RESPONSE: Two friends push together.
OUTCOME: The gate opens.
LESSON: Working together helps us solve problems.
PROVE IT: Use two details from the story.
Watch out: A theme is a full sentence for everyone, not a plot summary or just one word.

TEXT:
Title: THEME
Subtitle: What life lesson does the story teach?
TOPIC: friendship
THEME: Friends help each other through difficult times.
Follow the clues:
CHALLENGE → RESPONSE → OUTCOME → LESSON
CHALLENGE: A heavy garden gate will not open.
RESPONSE: Two friends push together.
OUTCOME: The gate opens.
LESSON: Working together helps us solve problems.
PROVE IT: Use two details from the story.
Watch out: A theme is a full sentence for everyone, not a plot summary or just one word.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills
LAYOUT AND ILLUSTRATION:
A coherent three-panel illustrated mini-story follows two children facing a stuck garden gate, working together, and opening it. An arrow connects to an illuminated lesson card. At top topic as small label vs theme as full sentence. Lesson must visibly derive from actions. Bright welcoming garden, not dense boxed paragraphs.

items.name: Figurative Language
items.copy:
Title: FIGURATIVE LANGUAGE
Subtitle: Picture the meaning behind the words.
SIMILE — Compare with like or as.
"The airship floated like a silver whale."
METAPHOR — Say one thing IS another.
"The garden was a sleeping giant."
PERSONIFICATION — Give human actions to nonhuman things.
"The wind whispered."
HYPERBOLE — Exaggerate for effect.
"I waited a million years!"
IDIOM — A saying with a special meaning.
"Break a leg!" means "Good luck!"
SOUND DEVICES
ALLITERATION — Repeated beginning sounds: "silent, silver sky."
ONOMATOPOEIA — A word that sounds like its sound: "buzz," "creak," "whoosh."
Ask: What does it really mean? What effect does it create?
Watch out: "I like apples" is not a simile.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Character
items.copy:
Title: CHARACTER
Subtitle: What do the clues reveal?
Use S.T.E.A.L.
S — SPEECH: What does the character say?
T — THOUGHTS: What does the character think?
E — EFFECT ON OTHERS: How do others react?
A — ACTIONS: What does the character do?
L — LOOKS: What does body language show?
TRAIT: What someone is usually like.
FEELING: An emotion right now.
MOTIVATION: Why someone acts.
Example: Lina keeps helping her friend even when the work is hard.
Trait: loyal. Feeling: tired. Motivation: to support her friend.
TRACK CHANGE: Beginning → Challenge → End
Watch out: One angry moment does not prove an angry personality.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Literary Elements
items.copy:
Title: LITERARY ELEMENTS
Subtitle: Build the story, then connect the parts.
CHARACTERS — Who is in the story?
SETTING — Where and when?
CONFLICT — What is the main problem?
PLOT — How do events unfold?
POINT OF VIEW — Who tells the story?
First person: I, we. Third person: he, she, they.
GENRE — What kind of text is it?
Adventure • Fantasy • Realistic fiction • Myth • Drama • Poetry
THE PLOT MOUNTAIN
Exposition → Rising action → Climax → Falling action → Resolution
Climax = the turning point.
Conflict may be against another character, nature, society, or oneself.
Watch out: The climax decides the conflict; it is not simply the loudest event.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Elements of Poetry
items.copy:
Title: ELEMENTS OF POETRY
Subtitle: Read aloud. Notice structure, sound, and meaning.
LINE — One row of words.
STANZA — A group of lines.
Example stanza:
The rain begins to fall. (A)
Upon the garden wall. (A)
The seeds wake up below. (B)
And start to stretch and grow. (B)
RHYME SCHEME: AABB
RHYTHM — The beat you hear.
METER — A regular pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables.
REPETITION — Words or sounds repeated for emphasis.
REFRAIN — A line or stanza that returns regularly.
IMAGERY — Words that appeal to the senses.
SPEAKER — The voice in the poem; not always the poet.
FREE VERSE — No regular rhyme or meter.
Watch out: Rhyme follows SOUND, not spelling.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Elements of Drama
items.copy:
Title: ELEMENTS OF DRAMA
Subtitle: A story written to be performed.
CAST — The characters in the play.
DIALOGUE — The words characters speak.
STAGE DIRECTIONS — Actions, feelings, setting, or sound.
SCENES & ACTS — Parts that build the play.
Read a tiny script:
Cast: LINA, BEN
Scene 1: Outside a locked garden.
LINA: (whispering) I found a key.
BEN: (smiling) Let's try the gate.
Scene 2: Inside the garden, later.
LINA: (looking around) We can bring it back to life.
NOTICE THE CHANGE
The scene changes time and place.
Watch out: Actors do not speak the stage directions aloud.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Text Evidence
items.copy:
Title: TEXT EVIDENCE
Subtitle: Prove your answer with details.
READ:
The airship rocked in the wind. Captain Osei held the wheel steady and spoke in a quiet voice.
QUESTION:
How can you tell the captain is calm?
ANSWER:
The captain stays calm during the storm.
EVIDENCE:
He "held the wheel steady" and "spoke in a quiet voice."
EXPLAIN:
Steady actions and a quiet voice show self-control.
ANSWER → EVIDENCE → EXPLAIN
Find a relevant detail. Quote or paraphrase accurately. Connect it to your answer.
Watch out: Choose a detail that PROVES the idea, not one that only shares the topic.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills

items.name: Vocabulary in Context
items.copy:
Title: VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
Subtitle: Use nearby clues to unlock meaning.
DEFINITION — The text tells the meaning.
"Seeds germinate, or begin to grow."
EXAMPLE — Details show what it looks like.
"The restless kitten paced and pawed at the door."
CONTRAST — Opposite ideas give a clue.
"Unlike the calm sea, the bay was restless."
SITUATION — Actions and events reveal meaning.
"Nell hesitated. She raised her hand to knock, then paused."
TRY IT:
"Trees grew densely, their branches crowded close together."
Densely means packed closely together.
READ AROUND → INFER → SUBSTITUTE → CHECK
Watch out: Choose the meaning used in THIS sentence.
Footer: Grade 5 • Module 2 • Reading Skills
